about: T1.33 part 3 (written by the package's independent test author, before the implementation), on the owner's answers of 2026-10-14 (items 24 and 26). The types' rows (P1B-43, the big-integer rule) are contract/type-set-vectors.json's, those with `cells`, read by the same test; these are its controls and the text_time rows. Each row adds a column `column` to contract/bases.yaml's `shop` `users` by its `witness`, the DuckDB statements run after shop's, and runs nested.list-int's case on rust-host through real DuckDB (rust/crates/sdm-testkit/tests/t133p3_reads.rs). `want`: the column described with `dtype` as the wire names it (and `stype`, and the table's `time_column`, where given); and its cells in the predict call's body: `cast`, each row's cell equal to DuckDB's own CAST(column AS VARCHAR) for that user (a number's cell as its text, so exact), `null`, every cell null, as the core sends a time of day, or none checked. The varint-key rows (fix round 1) instead make the key itself, users.user_id and orders.user_id, a VARINT, `column` the key, so materialize's seed joins run on it in each big-integer tier. The key rows of round 2 (`want.joins`: "own") also hold every users and orders row of each instance, in the body's predict and context, to that instance's own user: a seed join matching a key it does not equal puts another user's rows there. Expected values come from DuckDB at run time, never written here. The reference's answers for the text rows were probed with contract/tools/nested_type_record.py's run in the reference environment (DuckDB 1.5.6).

witness: CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE users AS SELECT *, 'w' || user_id::VARCHAR AS f FROM users
rows.why: a control: text with no setting, each cell DuckDB's own text, as the UUID and BIT rows are held

witness: CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE users AS SELECT *, user_id::HUGEINT * 1000 AS f FROM users
rows.why: a control: a HUGEINT with no setting (decimal128(38, 0)) read as a number today, each cell exact, as the lossless numbers are held

witness: CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE users AS SELECT *, ('12:0' || user_id::VARCHAR || ':00')::TIME AS f FROM users
rows.why: the core's time of day today, with no setting: TIMETZ under the setting is held to the same

witness: CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE users AS SELECT *, (['up to 12 weeks', 'Baseline and 6 months', 'Day 1 through Day 28', '24 hours post-dose'])[user_id % 4 + 1] AS time_frame FROM users
rows.why: text_time (owner, item 24): rel-trial's outcomes.time_frame, a name that says time over values that are no times, is text; the reference describes it string, categorical, no time column

witness: CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE users AS SELECT *, (['Prospective', 'Retrospective'])[user_id % 2 + 1] AS time_perspective FROM users
rows.why: text_time: rel-trial's designs.time_perspective is text; the reference describes it string, categorical

witness: CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE users AS SELECT *, strftime(DATE '2024-01-01' + user_id::INTEGER, '%Y-%m-%d') AS time_frame FROM users
rows.why: kept: a time-named column whose values read as times is still a time column; the reference describes it string, timestamp, the time column

witness: CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE orders AS SELECT * REPLACE ((CASE WHEN user_id = 7 THEN '7' ELSE user_id::VARCHAR END)::VARINT AS user_id) FROM orders
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE users AS SELECT * EXCLUDE (user_id), (CASE WHEN user_id = 7 THEN '7' ELSE user_id::VARCHAR END)::VARINT AS user_id FROM users
rows.why: a control: users.user_id and orders.user_id VARINT (no setting), every value fitting int64: the key received int64, materialize's seed joins on DuckDB succeed, each key cell exact (passed at 08c531b5, the subagent's probe)

witness: CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE orders AS SELECT * REPLACE ((CASE WHEN user_id = 7 THEN '100000000000000000000' ELSE user_id::VARCHAR END)::VARINT AS user_id) FROM orders
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE users AS SELECT * EXCLUDE (user_id), (CASE WHEN user_id = 7 THEN '100000000000000000000' ELSE user_id::VARCHAR END)::VARINT AS user_id FROM users
rows.why: the subagent's P2-1 (T1.33 part 3 review): the same VARINT key with user 7's id 10^20, so the key is received decimal128(38, 0); the seeds reach DuckDB in that tier, and the seed join ON t.user_id = s.seed_key (sdm-data/src/duckdb.rs's neighbors and lookup) has no DECIMAL(38,0) -> BIGNUM cast: materialize must succeed with each key cell exact, never an unnamed PROVIDER_ERROR

witness: CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE orders AS SELECT * REPLACE ((CASE WHEN user_id = 7 THEN '1000000000000000000000000000000000000000000' ELSE user_id::VARCHAR END)::VARINT AS user_id) FROM orders
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE users AS SELECT * EXCLUDE (user_id), (CASE WHEN user_id = 7 THEN '1000000000000000000000000000000000000000000' ELSE user_id::VARCHAR END)::VARINT AS user_id FROM users
rows.why: a control: the same VARINT key with user 7's id 10^42, past 38 digits, so received utf8; VARINT against VARCHAR compares in DuckDB, so materialize succeeds, each key cell exact (passed at 08c531b5, the subagent's probe)

witness: SET arrow_lossless_conversion = true

CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE orders AS SELECT * REPLACE ((CASE WHEN user_id = 6 THEN 18446744073709551617::UHUGEINT WHEN user_id = 7 THEN 18446744073709551618::UHUGEINT ELSE user_id::UHUGEINT END) AS user_id) FROM orders

CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE users AS SELECT * EXCLUDE (user_id), (CASE WHEN user_id = 6 THEN 18446744073709551617::UHUGEINT WHEN user_id = 7 THEN 18446744073709551618::UHUGEINT ELSE user_id::UHUGEINT END) AS user_id FROM users
rows.why: the subagent's round 2 P1: a lossless UHUGEINT key (users.user_id and orders.user_id) received decimal128(38, 0), users 6 and 7 holding 2^64+1 and 2^64+2, which differ in their low bits only; DuckDB 1.5.6 holds CAST(2^64+1 AS UHUGEINT) = CAST(2^64+2 AS HUGEINT) true, so a seed cast to HUGEINT joins each to the other's rows. Each instance's users and orders rows must be its own user's

rows.why: the same UHUGEINT key with users 6 and 7 holding 10^37 and 10^37+1, also equal to each other against a HUGEINT seed on DuckDB 1.5.6: each instance's rows must be its own user's
